meeting_header:
Date: 2026-11-05
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 60 minutes
Attendees: Olivia Chen (Redwood AE), Mateo Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (Nebulon Head of ML), Daniel Kwan (Nebulon Eng Manager), Elena Rodriguez (Nebulon Data Scientist)
summary: POC scoping focused on model selection for an open-model pilot, workload sizing (latency/throughput targets), benchmarking plan, and timelines. Customer needs multilingual support and domain-specific accuracy in financial/market analysis. Agreement to run 2-week pilot with three shortlisted models and share benchmark harness and datasets.
topics: POC success criteria and evaluation metrics
Open-model shortlist and tradeoffs (quality vs cost)
Benchmarks, datasets, and timeline for POC
transcript:
[00:00] Olivia: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we're gonna run through the POC scope for open models, real quick intros?
[00:07] Priya: hi I'm Priya, head of ML at Nebulon, we focus on deep market signal extraction, uh lots of multi-lingual data (en, zh, es), and need high factuality for reports.
[00:18] Daniel: Dan here, engineering manager, main constraints: 250ms median latency for short prompts, and we run ~2k reqs/min in peak.
[00:27] Mateo: thanks, Mateo from Redwood, i'll go over perf baselines and the harness we'll use. quick note, transcription might mangle some product names.
[00:36] Elena: Elena, data science — we'll provide labelled QA pairs and a set of multilingual docs.
[00:44] Olivia: ok cool, first question — success criteria, Priya what does a successful POC look like?
[00:50] Priya: two things, quality and economics. Quality: pass our QA test with F1 > 0.85 and less than 5% hallucination on the sampled set. Latency: for short queries (<=128 tokens) p95 < 350ms ideally, p95 < 500ms acceptable. Cost: cost per 1k completions under our internal threshold — um we'll share that number in the doc.
[01:18] Mateo: noted. for throughput you mentioned 2k reqs/min peak, we should clarify token distribution; short prompts vs long completions changes batch behaviors.
[01:28] Daniel: 70% short queries (~64 tokens), 20% medium (~256 tokens), 10% long (~1k tokens) — that's our rough split.
[01:40] Mateo: perfect, that helps with batching config. For the shortlist we propose running a quick baseline on three open variants: Mistral-Instruct 7B (quantized q4), Llama-3 8B (we'll test 8-bit/q4 variants), and Falcon-40B (fp16).
[01:56] Priya: quick interjection — we saw Llama-2-13B fine-tuned work pretty well for some vendors, is that in scope?
[02:03] Olivia: we can include Llama-2-13B as a fallback if you want, but our focus is on the cost/quality sweet spot for open models. Llama-3-8B tends to be strong on instruction tuning and multilingual quality.
[02:15] Elena: on multilingual, Chinese is critical — we need tests in zh and es as well. How do these models compare?
[02:22] Mateo: from benching we've seen Mistral variants are great in european languages, Llama-3 has stronger multilingual consistency including zh in many cases, Falcon tends to be hit/miss on non-en. we'll run targeted evals.
[02:36] Daniel: security thing — we need to know about data handling for hosted vs dedicated. we prefer dedicated for the pilot if possible.
[02:44] Olivia: understood. Dedicated gives you predictable capacity and data isolation; we'll send dedicated pilot pricing. For PII and audit, we support KMS integration, audit logs and SOC2 docs — i'll attach the security pack.
[02:58] Priya: good. Benchmarks — what will Redwood run vs what we run?
[03:03] Mateo: Redwood will run the runtime-level perf tests on our infra (same model variants, quant configs) to measure latency p50/p95, memory footprint, tokens/sec, and cost-per-token. We'll also run end-to-end tests from your network if you want (we can set up a temporary endpoint). You'll run the QA accuracy/hallucination eval and share results.
[03:21] Olivia: and we'll use the same harness and seed sets so numbers align. We'll post the harness to a repo link.
[03:28] Priya: timeline?
[03:30] Olivia: propose: today we align on scope. By 2026-11-09 you share datasets and success thresholds. Redwood runs baseline perf by 2026-11-12. Kickoff for the 2-week hands-on pilot on 2026-11-15. Final review meeting week of 2026-11-29. Does that work?
[03:49] Daniel: yep, that works for eng.
[03:51] Elena: yes.
[03:52] Priya: ok.
[03:54] Mateo: a couple of tradeoffs to call out: quantized 7B or 8B models (q4_0/q4o) usually meet your latency targets with much lower cost, but extreme quant can impact QA F1 by a few points on niche finance terms. Larger models like Falcon-40B are better on some long-context factuals but cost and memory are higher, and you might not meet p95 latency without dedicated GPUs.
[04:17] Priya: that's fair, we care more about factuality on financial terms than occasional latency — but need predictable SLOs.
[04:25] Olivia: for predictable SLOs Dedicated is recommended. For hosted quick tests we can do it too but there can be variance. Also we can set routing policies to fallback to higher-capacity variants if latency or errors spike.
[04:38] Daniel: can you quantify expected latency numbers for each model with a typical 64-token prompt on dedicated infra?
[04:45] Mateo: rough ballpark on Redwood Dedicated (A100-class): Mistral-7B q4 ~ p95 180-220ms, Llama-3-8B q4 ~ p95 200-260ms, Falcon-40B fp16 ~ p95 300-420ms depending on sequence length and batching. These are approximate; we'll provide exact numbers in the baseline report.
[05:05] Priya: great. For the QA eval, what's the recommended pass/fail gates?
[05:10] Olivia: recommended: F1 >= 0.85, hallucination rate <= 5% on randomly sampled dev set, and manual spot-checks on 50 docs for critical finance terms. If a model fails quality gate but meets cost and latency, we'll discuss model-specific tuning or prompt engineering as next step.
[05:27] Elena: on domain adaptation — do you offer fine-tuning or instruction-tuning on-prem?
[05:32] Olivia: we support a few flows: fine-tune on customer data in Dedicated, or retrieval-augmented generation with your vector DB. For POC we usually test RAG first; it's lower cost and faster to iterate.
[05:43] Priya: we'll prioritize RAG + prompt engineering initially. If that fails, we may consider a small finetune.
[05:49] Mateo: noted. instrumentation — we'll enable token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route so you can see economics by model and prompt type.
[05:59] Daniel: excellent. Any blockers?
[06:02] Priya: just internal approval for dedicated credit — we'll confirm by 2026-11-06.
[06:09] Olivia: ok we'll follow up with pricing + security pack. Mateo will post the benchmark harness repo and instructions.
[06:16] Elena: thanks everyone.
[06:18] Olivia: recap — action items (see follow-ups), agree on 2-week pilot starting 2026-11-15. Meeting adjourned.
[06:24] (end of recording)
